deepDive.title: Aquifer mechanics — how rocks store water
deepDive.body: Class 7 says groundwater lives in aquifers. Class 8 details how. AQUIFER = water-bearing rock. Two types: UNCONFINED (top layer porous, water table rises and falls with rain) and CONFINED (sandwiched between impermeable clay layers above and below — water is pressurised, sometimes flows out spontaneously when drilled = ARTESIAN well). POROSITY = % of rock that's empty space (sand: ~40%, granite: ~1%). PERMEABILITY = how easily water flows through (sand: high; clay: very low even though porous!). Indian Indo-Gangetic alluvial plain has the world's richest aquifer system — vast, deep, recharged by Himalayan snowmelt + monsoon. Rajasthan's hard-rock aquifers are tiny in comparison. Why Punjab can pump and Rajasthan can't — geology matters.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11 introduces Darcy's law for groundwater flow rates.

deepDive.title: Hydrological cycle math — quantifying India's water budget
deepDive.body: Class 7 traces the water cycle qualitatively. Class 11 puts numbers on it. India's average annual rainfall: ~1170 mm × land area = ~4000 billion cubic metres (4 trillion m³). Of this: ~700 BCM evaporates immediately, ~1900 BCM becomes surface runoff (rivers), ~700 BCM percolates to groundwater. India USES ~700 BCM per year — but unevenly. Punjab pumps 250% of its groundwater recharge (huge deficit). Bihar pumps only 30% (huge surplus, partly polluted from arsenic). National Water Mission's GROUNDWATER MAPPING program (CGWB) tracks this district-by-district. Modern hydrologists treat groundwater as a bank account — withdrawals must equal deposits long-term. Currently India is in deficit at -120 BCM per year. Unsustainable.
deepDive.nextStepHint: JEE / UPSC tests groundwater balance equations and the National Water Policy.

deepDive.title: Drip vs flood irrigation — water efficiency engineering
deepDive.body: Class 7 introduces drip, sprinkler, flood. Class 10 quantifies efficiency. FLOOD irrigation: water spread over field, soaks in gradually. Efficiency: ~40% (rest evaporates, runs off, deep-percolates past root zone). Cheap to set up but wasteful. SPRINKLER: efficiency ~70-80%. Better. DRIP: thin pipes deliver water DROP BY DROP at plant roots, often buried slightly. Efficiency: ~95%. Negligible evaporation, no runoff. Result: same crop yield with HALF the water. Indian government's PMKSY scheme subsidises drip 80% for small farmers. Maharashtra grape farms running drip outproduce flood-irrigated farms 3:1 by yield per litre. The investment (₹50,000/acre) pays back in 2-3 years through water + labour savings.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11/12 environmental engineering covers precision irrigation + IoT-controlled drip systems.
